title: Ops Resilience: First Signs
description: Strange power readings across Singapore's grid. Too coordinated to be coincidence.
storyContext: It starts with a flicker. Substation readings spike and dip in a pattern matching no known fault. Your team pulls up the grid feed and the room goes quiet. Too coordinated for coincidence. Someone is inside the control systems.

callbacks.arc1-ch1:hybrid-partner: Your old NDP hosting partner calls first: "Our grid readings look wrong too." When they worry, you worry.

software-engineer.title: Set Up the Early Warning System
software-engineer.instruction: Wire the grid's control systems with monitoring before the intruder escalates. Order the steps.
software-engineer.hint: You can't spot 'unusual' without knowing 'normal' first.

items.label: Map every control device and how they connect
Install monitoring sensors on each device
Set alert levels — anything unusual triggers a warning
Wire alerts straight to the security team

software-engineer.consequenceSuccess: Tripwires armed. Twenty minutes later the first alert fires — now you're watching them, not the reverse.
software-engineer.consequenceFail: Alarms set before recording normal — they scream at everything. Wolf-crying sensors get ignored fast.

data-scientist.title: Estimate How Far It Has Spread
data-scientist.instruction: The graph shows the percentage of devices flagging weird activity at each check. If the trend holds, how many of the 200 control devices are compromised?
data-scientist.hint: Project the next percentage, then apply it to 200 devices.
data-scientist.consequenceSuccess: Your projection lands. Leadership finally grasps the scale — this isn't a glitch, it's an invasion.
data-scientist.consequenceFail: The spread outruns your estimate. Whoever this is, they move faster than the maths said.

cloud-engineer.title: Deploy the Detection Toolkit
cloud-engineer.instruction: The pattern matches nothing on record. Pick how to classify the threat before leadership responds.
cloud-engineer.hint: New threats fool tools trained only on old ones.

options.label: Run the automated threat detector. Answer in 5 minutes — but it only knows old attack patterns.
options.consequence: Five minutes later: "no known threat detected." Which is exactly what a brand-new threat looks like. Hmm.

options.label: Compare the pattern by hand against past incidents and intel. 30 minutes, high confidence.
options.consequence: Thirty careful minutes later you have a confident answer — and a knot in your stomach. It's real.

options.label: Run three different detection methods; majority verdict wins. Slower, far more reliable on new threats.
options.consequence: Two of three methods agree: coordinated intrusion. The third shrugs. Good enough to sound the alarm.

options.label: Share the pattern with partner cyber teams. Answer in 10 minutes — but you show your hand.
options.consequence: A partner team replies in eight minutes: "We've seen this. Brace yourselves." Sharing paid off — this time.
